top_strength: This is a model estimate build. Garrison opened with a real agenda and a time ask - "if you happen to have around five to ten minutes or so" - then ran a genuinely thorough inventory, chasing the rooms customers forget ("anything coming from maybe like the backyard area, porch patio") and pulling a box benchmark out of thin air when she could not guess. Then he did the hard, honest thing: he pre-framed the bad news before delivering it - "I think the estimate that I've got built out for you here is going to be a good bit higher than what you were initially quoted... I don't want you to feel any sort of sticker shock" - and justified every dollar of the gap by name (crib disassembly, appliances, the forty-minute fridge round-trip, fifty boxes). He also volunteered the cheaper Sunday-through-Thursday rate without being asked, and earned Save Your Ass with a concrete staging example: "we'll pull the truck right up to the garage... That's gonna save a whole heck a lot of time." She closed with "Thank you so much for the quote and kind of walking me through this."
coaching_note: He did everything except ask for the business. This customer was referred by a neighbor, called specifically to get it scheduled ("that's why I wanted to call in advance, so I can kind of get a quote and get it scheduled"), and had no objection left on the table - and Garrison still ended on "we look forward to hearing from you." A twenty-five minute consultative build should end with a direct close: the date is open, booking is free, rescheduling is free, want me to hold Saturday the tenth right now? The second gap is the differentiator block - on a move full of heavy gym equipment, a treadmill and appliances, No Worries Damage Coverage never came up once, and neither did Meet Your Mover or the On-Time Guarantee. Those three take sixty seconds and they are what justifies a $2,781 number against the online quote she is comparing it to.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm with natural affirmations, real empathy in the sticker-shock pre-frame, and a genuine rapport moment on the first-time-with-movers story ("Yeah, I hear that you can only do that for so long") - held back from a 5 only because he had her profile open and never once used her name.
